channel.title: Tobias Romero: All the Latest Rock and Metal News on Loud Legends
channel.description: Recent content in Tobias Romero: All the Latest Rock and Metal News on Loud Legends

item.title: BLACK SABBATH’s Founding Four Reunite Ahead of OZZY OSBOURNE’s Final Show; First Photos Released
item.description: The original members of Black Sabbath have reunited to rehearse for one last performance. Ozzy Osbourne, Geezer Butler, Tony Iommi, and Bill Ward are preparing for their farewell event, “Back To The Beginning: Ozzy’s Final Bow”, which takes place on July 5 at Villa Park in Birmingham, England.

item.title: ASKING ALEXANDRIA Responds to Criticism With Instagram Post: 'It's Never F-cking Good Enough'
item.description: Asking Alexandria has drawn attention again, this time through a post on their official Instagram. The band shared a video clip of frontman Danny Worsnop performing the song “Things Could Be Different” during their recent Warped Tour appearance in Washington, D.

item.title: KORN’s Full PINKPOP 2007 Performance With SLIPKNOT’s JOEY JORDISON Released On YouTube
item.description: A professionally filmed video of KORN’s full set at the Pinkpop Festival in the Netherlands — recorded on May 28, 2007 — has been made available online via the Pinkpop Archive YouTube channel.

item.title: LORNA SHORE Releases 'Unbreakable' Single and Music Video: 'It Will Never Break Us Down'
item.description: Lorna Shore has dropped a new single, “Unbreakable”, along with a fresh music video, giving fans another preview of their next album, I Feel The Everblack Festering Within Me.

item.title: OZZY OSBOURNE Says He Wants To Work With PAUL MCCARTNEY: 'I Would Be Honoured'
item.description: During a new episode of Ozzy Speaks on SiriusXM (transcribed by LOUDLEGENDS.COM), Ozzy Osbourne mentioned that he would like to collaborate with Paul McCartney. The rock icon discussed the idea while chatting with his co-host, Billy Morrison.

item.title: OZZY OSBOURNE Honored With New 'Working Class Hero' Display in Hometown
item.description: A new exhibition honoring Ozzy Osbourne is now open in his hometown of Birmingham, England. The “Working Class Hero” exhibit launched Wednesday (June 25) at the Birmingham Museum & Art Gallery.

item.title: The Lemonheads Drop New Single “In The Margin,” Share Details on First Album in Nearly 20 Years
item.description: After years of writing, drifting, and starting over, Evan Dando is back. The Lemonheads are set to release their first studio album in almost two decades, titled Love Chant, arriving October 24 via Fire Records.

item.title: AC/DC Faces Backlash Over Viral Tour Footage As Fans Call For Retirement: 'Painful'
item.description: Footage from a recent AC/DC concert is making waves online, and not in the way the band might hope. A TikTok video from the group’s May 4 performance at Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, Massachusetts, has gone viral (watch it below).

item.title: The Emotional METALLICA Song That Wasn’t Meant to Be, According to JAMES HETFIELD
item.description: When Load dropped in June 1996, it marked a sharp left turn for Metallica. The band traded speed and aggression for a slower, more reflective sound. That shift didn’t land well with everyone, but it did show fans a broader side of the band’s musical identity.

item.title: ASKING ALEXANDRIA Fans Question Danny Worsnop’s Performance, Call for His Exit
item.description: Asking Alexandria’s recent Warped Tour performance is stirring debate online, and some fans think it may be time for lead singer Danny Worsnop to step aside. The band’s subreddit lit up after their June 15 set, with over a dozen posts and hundreds of comments discussing Worsnop’s vocals and stage presence.

item.title: Sodom's TOM ANGELRIPPER On Modern Metal Production: 'It's Cheap And It Shows'
item.description: Tom Angelripper has no patience for how modern metal is made. From his perspective, today’s studio habits cut corners and it’s obvious. “Recording in a digital way is cheap,” he said (via Blabbermouth).

item.title: EUGENE ABDUKHANOV On MESHUGGAH's Early Days: 'People Didn’t Get It Then'
item.description: Eugene Abdukhanov isn’t new to giving credit where it’s due, even if it takes the rest of the world a couple of decades to catch up. Sitting down with Forever Loud at Download Festival, the JINJER bassist pulled no punches while looking back on what it was like watching MESHUGGAH rise from being the metal kid no one invited to the party, to becoming the very sound system (transcribed by BLABBERMOUTH.

item.title: The BEST SONG to Introduce Someone to KORN, According to JONATHAN DAVIS
item.description: So you want to introduce someone to Korn. Good luck. You’ve got nearly three decades’ worth of dreadlocks, detuned guitars, and unresolved childhood trauma to work with.

item.title: FIT FOR A KING Announces New Album 'LONELY GOD', Shares Lead Single And Tracklist
item.description: Fit For A King have unveiled Lonely God, their eighth studio album, scheduled to arrive August 1, 2025 via Solid State Records. The announcement came with a music video (available at the end of this article) for the blistering title track, which showcases the band’s signature blend of gnarly riffs, guttural growls, heavy grooves, and a dash of industrial crunch.

item.title: REVOCATION Announces New Album 'New Gods, New Masters' With Guest Appearances From Cattle Decapitation, Gorguts, And More
item.description: Revocation will release their ninth studio album, New Gods, New Masters, on September 26 via Metal Blade Records. It’s their fifth record under the label and the follow-up to 2022’s Netherheaven.

item.title: The Day KORN Knocked a Guy Out Mid-Show… and Then WROTE A SONG About It
item.description: Not every song is born in a studio with clean instruments and sober minds. Some, like Korn’s Clown, crawl out of drug-fueled all-nighters in dingy apartments, shaped as much by the chaos around them as by the riffs themselves.

item.title: OZZY OSBOURNE Jokes About DNA Sale With Liquid Death: 'Clone Me, You Bastards'
item.description: Liquid Death has cranked up its marketing chaos once again. This time, the company is selling cans that not only once contained iced tea but also hold something far weirder: Ozzy Osbourne’s DNA.

item.title: JAMES HETFIELD On His Father's Abandonment: 'He Didn't Even Say Goodbye'
item.description: Before the arenas, awards, and global tours, James Hetfield was just a kid growing up in the suburbs of Los Angeles. The setting looked ideal from the outside.

item.title: Motörhead Releases 'Leavin’ Here' Video From Recently Discovered 1976 Tapes
item.description: After nearly five decades of dust, decay, and general disregard, Motörhead has cracked open the time capsule no one saw coming. The band has just dropped a music video for “Leavin’ Here”, a snarling slab of rock that also happens to be one of the oldest recordings from the Lemmy–Eddie Clarke–Phil Taylor era.

item.title: Vogg Says Decapitated’s New Album is Halfway Done, But When Will It Drop?
item.description: OKAY, SO—Vogg, the guitar wizard of Decapitated, has somehow managed to write 50% of the band’s new album. Fifty. Percent. Not 49%. Not 51%. Exactly half. And he dropped this information like it was no big deal while floating on the 70000 Tons of Metal cruise, which, if you don’t know, is basically a lawless, floating metal festival where dehydration, questionable decisions, and ear-shattering riffs collide on the high seas.

item.title: Clown Admits He Was a “Naysayer” About Revisiting Slipknot’s First Album
item.description: It’s 2025, and somehow Slipknot is still here, still wearing masks, still smashing percussion instruments like cavemen discovering fire, but also—shockingly—getting reflective about their past. Yes, you read that right: Shawn “Clown” Crahan, the band’s resident chaos conductor, actually sat down and got nostalgic.

item.title: AVANTASIA’s 'Here Be Dragons' Features KAMELOT’s Tommy Karevik on New Single The Witch
item.description: Well, folks, let me tell ya’ll, Tobias Sammet is back with another Avantasia album, and this time he’s gone full medieval cartographer on us. The tenth studio album, Here Be Dragons, is set to release on February 28, 2025, via Napalm Records, and based on everything we know, it’s shaping up to be either a symphonic masterpiece or the musical equivalent of a Renaissance Fair gone horribly wrong.

item.title: The Callous Daoboys Announce New Album "I Don’t Want to See You in Heaven"
item.description: Let me set the scene for ya: It’s 2 AM, I’ve had too much coffee, and I’m staring at my laptop like it owes me money. Somewhere in Atlanta, The Callous Daoboys are probably plotting their next auditory crime, gearing up to unleash I Don’t Want to See You in Heaven on May 16 via MNRK Heavy.

item.title: Lorraine Lewis on Joining OnlyFans: "It’s Sexy, I’m Owning It, And I’m Having Fun!"
item.description: Lorraine Lewis. 66 years old. Rock icon. Ex-VIXEN. Current FEMME FATALE badass. Also? Now officially on OnlyFans. And not just dipping her toes in—she’s fully in the pool.

item.title: The End of an Era: Ozzy Osbourne’s Final Performance with Black Sabbath Announced
item.description: You ever notice how bands never actually retire? They announce their very last, totally final, we swear on our drummer’s snare collection concert… and then five years later—boom.

item.title: Arch Enemy's Alissa White-Gluz on Veganism, Metal, and Life on the Road: “Super Easy”
item.description: Vegan. Straight edge. Death metal vocalist. Alissa White-Gluz of Arch Enemy is not exactly what you’d call your average rockstar. And yet, despite what some might assume about a life of touring (hotel food, fast food, or whatever’s closest and cheapest), she’s been managing just fine—on plants.

item.title: Jon Oliva Says New Savatage Album is Nearly Complete—But Can He Ever Perform Again?
item.description: Twenty years. That’s how long it’s been since Savatage last did a proper tour. Two decades of silence, barring the occasional “We might do something soon” tease. Well, guess what?

item.title: Sharon den Adel Confirms Within Temptation’s Next Album Is Taking Shape: “We Have a Clear Vision”
item.description: So Within Temptation has a plan. Well, sort of. Sharon den Adel insists they “really have an idea what we wanna do next,” which sounds promising—until you realize that the band started with the intention of taking their sweet time, only to immediately flip-flop.

item.title: GOJIRA Wins 2025 Grammy for Olympic Performance Song ‘Mea Culpa (Ah! Ça ira!)’
item.description: GOJIRA. Grammy winners. Sounds nice—doesn’t it? Took long enough. But yeah man—it finally happened. The French metal titans bagged the 2025 Best Metal Performance Grammy for Mea Culpa (Ah!

item.title: NIGHTWISH Goes Behind-the-Scenes with 'Yesterwynde' Doc; VIDEO
item.description: NIGHTWISH, the masters of symphonic bombast, have dropped a 45-minute documentary that peels back the layers of their latest opus, “Yesterwynde.” Released on September 20, this album wraps up the trilogy that kicked off with “Endless Forms Most Beautiful” in 2015.

item.title: System of a Down Tease Fans with Cryptic 'Chop Suey!' Post
item.description: The legendary metal misfits have stirred the pot again. Hot on the heels of announcing three summer shows with heavyweights like KoRn, Avenged Sevenfold, and Deftones, they pulled a classic move: double the dates, double the hype.

item.title: Jim Root Pushes for Slipknot’s "Look Outside Your Window" Release
item.description: The wait for Look Outside Your Window has dragged on so long, it’s practically become folklore at this point. A decade or more of teasing, false promises, and cryptic updates, and here we are, still empty-handed.

item.title: SLUDGE METAL Veterans ACID BATH Announce 2025 Shows
item.description: The big reveal for Louder Than Life? Acid Bath joins Slayer as one of the first bands confirmed for the festival. A bold pairing, but hey, you need at least one band to keep things grimy.

item.title: Festival Canceled: Sick New World 2025 Won’t Happen
item.description: Looks like Sick New World 2025 is joining the growing list of festivals that never make it past the announcement phase. Scheduled for April 12, 2025, in Las Vegas, this highly-hyped event has been officially scrapped.

item.title: As I Lay Dying's Comeback Album Mysteriously Disappears From Streaming
item.description: Mysterious times for As I Lay Dying fans. The band’s 2019 comeback album, Shaped By Fire, has all but vanished from streaming platforms, and the silence around its absence just adds to the mystery.

item.title: Watch: DREAM THEATER Releases 'Night Terror' Video Ahead of 'Parasomnia' Album
item.description: February 7, 2025, marks the arrival of DREAM THEATER’s sixteenth album, “Parasomnia,” via InsideOut Music. This time, they’ve reunited with their prodigal son, drummer Mike Portnoy, whose last contribution to the band dates back to 2009’s “Black Clouds & Silver Linings.

item.title: Scott Stapp Reflects on Sobriety: "Drinking is No Longer an Option"
item.description: Scott Stapp isn’t dancing around the issue of sobriety. At this point in his life, drinking is, quite simply, off the table. When asked whether it’s challenging to stay sober on something as indulgent as a cruise, particularly the band’s “Summer Of ‘99” cruises, he doesn’t hesitate: “No, it’s not.

item.title: Roger Miret Opens Up His Hardcore Archives in "With Time"
item.description: Roger Miret isn’t one for nostalgia tours. But in his new book, “Agnostic Front With Time: The Roger Miret Archives”, he takes us back to the gritty streets of 1980s New York City, where hardcore punk wasn’t a scene — it was survival.

item.title: SKILLET's John Cooper on Political Divides in Rock: "We're Shut Out"
item.description: In a recent chat with the Rebellious Remarks podcast, John Cooper, frontman for SKILLET, took the opportunity to drop some of his usual truth bombs about being a Christian rock musician in today’s ultra-polarized world.

item.title: Ted Nugent Praises Metallica’s "Soulful" Groove While Criticizing Pantera
item.description: In a recent episode of Ted Nugent’s show “Spirit Campfire” on Real America’s Voice, the ever-outspoken Nugent threw a nod to several rockers who are still out there tearing up stages, mentioning Mark Farner, STYX, and Sammy Hagar as some of the enduring performers.

item.title: 'Master Of Puppets' Wins Out for Shavo Odadjian in METALLICA Album Showdown
item.description: When Shavo Odadjian, bassist of SYSTEM OF A DOWN, got hit with the impossible question of whether METALLICA’s “Ride The Lightning” or “Master Of Puppets” was the superior album during an interview with Radioactive MikeZ on 96.

item.title: KORN’s Brian 'Head' Welch on Mortality: "I Want to Die in a Bed, Not On Stage"
item.description: Brian “Head” Welch from KORN isn’t buying into the whole “die on stage” fantasy. Asked recently about his 2014 comment—where he hinted at retiring by 60—he didn’t exactly backpedal.

item.title: Watch: Korn Performs "Hey Daddy" Live for First Time Since 1999
item.description: Korn pulled a fast one last night. “Hey Daddy”—yep, that’s right. Played live for the first time since 1999. This wasn’t just a random throwback either. September 12, Tampa, Florida.

item.title: AS I LAY DYING Announces Eighth Album 'Through Storms Ahead'
item.description: Two and a half decades and a pile of albums later, AS I LAY DYING is tossing another entry onto their discography stack. Their eighth studio album, “Through Storms Ahead”, hits shelves (or playlists, let’s be honest) on November 15, 2024, courtesy of Napalm Records.

item.title: Slipknot’s Touring Playbook is Getting a Shake-Up, Says Corey Taylor
item.description: Slipknot’s endless cycle of tours has always begged the question: how do they breathe between the chaos? For Corey Taylor, who’s juggling Slipknot, solo projects, and Stone Sour, the answer is becoming increasingly clear, he doesn’t.

item.title: Countdown Chaos: Is Deryck Whibley Joining Linkin Park?
item.description: The countdown on Linkin Park’s site is ticking, and fans are losing their minds. Again. What is it this time? A new song? A reunion? Nope. The latest theory says Deryck Whibley from Sum 41 is sliding in as their new frontman.

item.title: Mike Shinoda Teases “Exciting Things” for Linkin Park Fans
item.description: Reunions? Overdone. Predictable. (Unless it’s the one band you care about—then it’s “historic” and “world-changing,” right?) For years now, Linkin Park has been the one nu-metal heavyweight keeping quiet, while every other act rides the nostalgia wave like it’s 2001.

item.title: Metallica’s Ride the Lightning Sales Surge 160% Amid 40th Anniversary
item.description: Calling Metallica one of the biggest-selling bands in music is almost redundant at this point. With albums like the Black Album still lingering on Billboard charts and streaming relentlessly decades later, the band’s impact is as constant as it is undeniable.

item.title: Phil Labonte: Korn’s Impact on Deathcore Goes Beyond Nu-Metal
item.description: When a band ends up becoming so influential that people start crediting them for launching a whole subgenre, it’s something to take note of. But when a group gets blamed for a genre they don’t even directly belong to?

item.title: Slipknot Celebrates 25 Years at Knotfest Brazil; See Details
item.description: Back in 1999, we were all panicking about Y2K taking down the world’s tech, arguing over a president’s private escapades instead of governmental coups, and gleefully downloading Metallica tracks despite their infamous Napster tantrum.

item.title: AS I LAY DYING Finalizes New Record Deal for 2024 Album
item.description: When Tim Lambesis sat down with Jamey Jasta on the “The Jasta Show”, the HATEBREED frontman probably knew he’d get some juicy tidbits on AS I LAY DYING’s new material.

item.title: Brian Welch on Korn's New Album: “The Heaviest in Years”
item.description: Brian “Head” Welch is dropping those familiar lines again—“heaviest stuff in years,” you know the drill. It’s almost like there’s a secret musician handbook, and on page one, right under “never say your best days are behind you,” is this classic line.

item.title: Korn Announces 30th Anniversary Concert with Star-Studded Lineup
item.description: Korn isn’t one to let their 30th anniversary of that self-titled debut just slip by quietly. They’ve decided to throw a massive bash at BMO Stadium in Los Angeles on October 5, 2024.

item.title: Watch: Korn Meets Vanessa Carlton in a Bizarre Mashup
item.description: Just when you thought the world had run out of odd musical combinations, along comes YouTuber mac glocky with a new creation. Fresh off his last “masterpiece”—a mashup of System of a Down and the B-52s—he’s back with another experiment: what happens when you blend Vanessa Carlton’s early 2000s pop hit “A Thousand Miles” with the nu-metal force of Korn?

item.title: Metallica’s M72 Tour Breaks SoFi Stadium’s Single-Show Record
item.description: Metallica just sent Taylor Swift’s attendance record at SoFi Stadium spinning. In a double dose of pure metal, Metallica managed to pull off a weekend showdown that drew fans from every corner, making sure to leave their mark.
